options.label: Put spread on QQQ · 1 month · 5% / 10% down
options.note: Cheapest cover for a 5–10% drawdown. Skew is steep, so the lower put you sell pays for a lot of the upper one.
options.scenario_note: Basket moves 1.6× NDX. The spread pays at most 3.1% of the basket (5 points × $62.4 of notional), so it softens a drawdown rather than stopping it; below −10% you are long the basket again.

options.label: Collar on QQQ · 1 month · sell 5% up, buy 5% down
options.note: Near-free, but you give up upside above +5%. Wrong tool while the basket is running.
options.scenario_note: Basket moves 1.6× NDX. The put pays 0.62% of the basket for each point NDX falls below −5%, and the call you sold takes the same off each point above +5%: at NDX −20% the book loses 22.8% instead of 32%, and at +10% it makes 12.7% instead of 16%.

options.label: Outright QQQ puts · 1 month · 5% down
options.note: Simplest, and twice the price. Vol is rich right now; you're paying for it.
options.scenario_note: Basket moves 1.6× NDX. The puts pay 0.62% of the basket for each point NDX falls below −5%, with no cap, but they cost 2.4% up front: they only beat the spread in a drop past about −12%.

why_index.label: Why index options, not the names
why_index.text: puts on NVDA and AVGO would cover what QQQ can't, a basket-specific selloff, but single-name vol runs 1.7× the index, so the outright puts' protection would cost about 4.1% (1.7 × 2.4%). The index hedge is the cheap one; it leaves the idiosyncratic leg open on purpose.

recommendation.label: Recommendation
recommendation.text: the put spread. For 1.1% of the basket it pays up to 3.1% in a 5–10% NDX drawdown, and it's the one that reads right against today's vol card: rich implied, steep skew. Sell the wing, don't buy the outright.
